You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system and the exact names your specification must define so that it binds to a fixed model-checking configuration. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior and defines exactly the named constants, variables, and operators listed below. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: This specification models Dijkstra's classical self-stabilizing token ring algorithm from EWD426. The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each storing a counter value in a bounded domain 0..M-1; node 0 can create a new token by incrementing relative to the last node, while every other node passes the token by copying its predecessor when their values differ. The spec assumes at least one node and a nonempty value domain, together with the condition N <= M + 1, and it verifies a stabilization property stating that eventually the system reaches and stays in a state with a unique token.
